questions.q: What did Yahweh tell Ezekiel to do with a sword and a scale?
questions.a: Yahweh told Ezekiel to shave his head and beard with the sword and then weigh the hair on the scale.

questions.q: What was Ezekiel to do with each third of his hair?
questions.a: Ezekiel was to burn a third in the city, strike a third with the sword around the city, and scatter a third to the wind.

questions.q: What did Yahweh tell Ezekiel to do with a few of the hairs?
questions.a: Yahweh told Ezekiel to tie a few of the hairs to his clothing.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say would happen after Ezekiel threw some hairs into the fire?
questions.a: Yahweh said a fire would go out from there to all the people of Israel.

questions.q: According to Yahweh, where is Jerusalem?
questions.a: Jerusalem is in the middle of all the nations.

questions.q: Why does Yahweh say Jerusalem has rebelled with more wickedness than the nations around her?
questions.a: Because the people of Jerusalem had all of Yahweh’s commands but rejected them and did not obey his laws.

questions.q: What does Yahweh say Jerusalem did not do?
questions.a: Yahweh says the people of Jerusalem did not live by his laws, nor do what he commanded, nor did they even follow the laws of the nations around them.

questions.q: What does Yahweh say he will do because of the nation of Israel’s behavior?
questions.a: Yahweh says he will act as an enemy against them and punish them while the other nations watch.

questions.q: What does Yahweh say he will do because of Jerusalem’s abominations?
questions.a: Yahweh says he will punish them as he has never done before and will never do again.

questions.q: What horrible things will the people of Israel do because of Yahweh’s judgment on them?
questions.a: Parents will eat their children, and children will eat their parents.

questions.q: Why does Yahweh say he is not going to save the people from punishment?
questions.a: Yahweh says he will not save them from punishment because they defiled his holy place with their unacceptable practices.

questions.q: What will Yahweh do with each third of the people?
questions.a: A third will die by plague or famine, a third will die from wounds, and a third will be scattered.

questions.q: What does Yahweh say will happen with his anger after this judgment?
questions.a: Yahweh says his anger will be fully expressed and he will calm himself after this judgment.

questions.q: What does Yahweh say he will make Jerusalem?
questions.a: Yahweh says he will make Jerusalem a ruin and a place that is mocked by the other nations around them.

questions.q: What will other people say about Jerusalem after Yahweh’s judgments?
questions.a: Other people will scorn and mock Jerusalem after Yahweh’s destruction of it.

questions.q: What does Yahweh say he will do to increase the famine?
questions.a: Yahweh says he will entirely take away their supply of food.

questions.q: What four things does Yahweh say he will send against Jerusalem?
questions.a: Yahweh says he will send famine, wild animals, plague, and the enemies against Jerusalem.

commentary.text: A type of hair, showing the judgments about to come upon the Jews. (Ezek. 5:1-4) These awful judgments are declared. (Ezek. 5:5-17)

Ezek. 5:1-4 The prophet must shave off the hair of his head and beard, which signifies God's utter rejecting and abandoning that people. One part must be burned in the midst of the city, denoting the multitudes that should perish by famine and pestilence. Another part was to be cut in pieces, representing the many who were slain by the sword. Another part was to be scattered in the wind, denoting the carrying away of some into the land of the conqueror, and the flight of others into the neighbouring countries for shelter. A small quantity of the third portion was to be bound in his shirts, as that of which he is very careful. But few were reserved. To whatever refuge sinners flee, the fire and sword of God's wrath will consume them.

Ezek. 5:5-17 The sentence passed upon Jerusalem is very dreadful, the manner of expression makes it still more so. Who is able to stand in God's sight when he is angry? Those who live and die impenitent, will perish for ever unpitied; there is a day coming when the Lord will not spare. Let not persons or churches, who change the Lord's statutes, expect to escape the doom of Jerusalem. Let us endeavour to adorn the doctrine of God our Saviour in all things. Sooner or later God's word will prove itself true.
